approved: Marriage Amendment (Celebrant Administration and Fees) Bill 2014
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would make Commonwealth-registered marriage celebrants pay an annual registration charge to recover the cost of regulating them.
Celebrants who do not pay the charge, unless exempted, would be deregistered, and regulations would set out exemption processes and grounds.
The charge would apply from 1 July 2013, and the amendments in Schedule 1, Part 4 would apply from 1 July 2014 or later.
Introduces cost recovery for regulating Commonwealth-registered marriage celebrants.
Requires celebrants to pay an annual registration charge or be deregistered.
Allows regulations to provide exemptions from the charge.
Requires aspiring celebrants to pay an application fee unless exempted.
Allows regulations to require a fee for applying for an exemption from professional development requirements.
Makes technical, transitional and administrative amendments to the Marriage Act.
Commonwealth-registered marriage celebrants, including those from independent religious organisations, and aspiring marriage celebrants.

Moved a bill to allow the government to charge Commonwealth-registered marriage celebrants an annual registration fee, with a statutory limit of $600 indexed to the consumer price index. Said the actual charge for the 2014-15 financial year would be considerably lower, at $240.

Moved a bill introducing cost recovery for the Marriage Celebrants Program, noting that 71.9 per cent of Australian marriages were performed by civil celebrants in 2012. Said celebrant numbers had grown from 3,334 in 2003 to over 10,400, and proposed a $240 annual registration charge alongside other fees.

Supported the Marriage Amendment celebrant bills, recounted the Marriage Celebrant Program's creation in 1973 under Attorney-General Lionel Murphy with celebrant Lois D'Arcy, noted 71 per cent of 2011 marriages were performed by celebrants, and pointed out the fees of $600, $240 and $30 in the bill match those he introduced as Attorney-General in 2013.

Referred the Marriage Amendment (Celebrant Registration Charge) Bill 2014 and the Marriage Amendment (Celebrant Administration and Fees) Bill 2014 to the Federation Chamber for further consideration, noting general agreement on the legislation.

Presented a report examining 22 bills and 42 legislative instruments for compatibility with human rights. Raised concerns that national uniform schemes negotiated through COAG can be agreed without formal human rights scrutiny, and sought an update on efforts to address this in drafting protocols for national legislation.

Introduced two marriage celebrant bills implementing cost-recovery fees from 1 July 2014, including a $600 registration application fee, a $240 annual celebrant registration charge, and a $30 fee for seeking an exemption, all indexed annually to CPI.
Marriage Amendment (Celebrant Administration and Fees) Act 2014
